sources.why_it_matters: Current comparative evidence on supplier-integrity and procurement-integrity measures; useful for distinguishing legal frameworks from implementation quality.

sources.org: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

sources.title: Interconnection of Large Loads to the Interstate Transmission System (Docket No. RM26-4-000)
sources.why_it_matters: Official FERC docket page for the large-load ANOPR on timely, orderly, and equitable integration of data-center and other significant loads into interstate transmission.

sources.title: Q4 2025 Release Tables: Shares of Wealth by Wealth Percentile Groups
sources.org: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis / Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.why_it_matters: Direct current DFA release-table extraction for U.S. total-net-worth shares: top 0.1, top 1, 90-99, 50-90, and bottom-50 groups. It closes the prior exact-share proof debt without treating aggregate Z.1 totals as distributional evidence.

sources.title: 2026 PJM Load Forecast Report
sources.why_it_matters: Official PJM forecast tying large-load adjustments, including data-center load, to zonal and RTO peak/net-energy growth; it turns the AI/data-center case from national demand projection into regional grid-incidence evidence.

sources.title: Commercial electricity sales have soared in Virginia, driven by data centers
sources.why_it_matters: Official EIA localization of the data-center grid burden: Virginia/Dominion-zone commercial sales and peak-load pressure create a concrete ratepayer, reliability, and place-public-finance incidence surface.

sources.title: PUCO orders AEP Ohio to create data center specific tariff
sources.why_it_matters: Official Ohio regulatory-order notice adopting a data-center tariff settlement for AEP Ohio; it turns the large-load cost-shift problem into an enforceable tariff/current-law incidence surface rather than a generic forecast concern.

sources.title: Data Center Tariff
sources.why_it_matters: Utility tariff implementation page specifying Schedule DCT thresholds, load-study fees, ramp period, contract term, collateral, minimum demand charges, reassignment conditions, behind-the-meter generation controls, and exit-fee mechanics.

sources.title: SCC Data Center Initiatives — Dominion Energy Virginia
sources.why_it_matters: Official Virginia SCC fact surface for Dominion data-center safeguards: GS-5 separate rate class, alternative cost allocation, 14-year contract obligation, 85% T&D minimum charges, collateral, and interconnection-review duties.

sources.title: PUC Advances Plan to Balance Data Center Growth and Consumer Protection
sources.why_it_matters: Official Pennsylvania PUC tentative-order notice for a statewide model tariff, including cost-causation measures, contributions-in-aid-of-construction, tiered collateral, minimum contract terms, low-income contributions, and flexible-service options.

sources.title: PSC Overhauls We Energies’ Data Center Tariff, Makes Improvements to Protect Existing Customers
sources.why_it_matters: Official Wisconsin PSC open-meeting decision notice for We Energies’ very-large-customer/data-center tariff: 15-year minimum term, 100 MW threshold, transmission-cost-shift revisions, 100% full-benefits resource model, reporting, and transparency requirements.

sources.title: PSC Ensures Stronger Public Transparency, Customer Protections in Review of Alliant Energy’s Data Center Service Agreement
sources.why_it_matters: Official Wisconsin PSC open-meeting decision notice for a Beaver Dam data-center electric-service agreement, adding project-level termination-charge, financial-safeguard, reporting, public-transparency, energy-program-contribution, and stand-alone future large-load-tariff requirements.

sources.title: Statement in Support of CAUSE-PA to Joint Petition for Approval of Non-Unanimous Settlement, PPL Electric rate case
sources.org: Pennsylvania Utility Law Project / Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission docket record
sources.why_it_matters: Detailed Pennsylvania rate-case record for PPL Electric large-load LP-6 settlement terms: 50 MW/75 MW threshold, 10-year electric service agreements, enhanced credit/security, mandatory exit fees, CIAC/security for upgrades, segmentation of non-critical load, reporting, and low-income USR assignment to LP-6.

sources.title: PUC Issues Decision in PPL Electric Rate Proceeding
sources.why_it_matters: Current Pennsylvania approval surface for the PPL settlement: confirms final PUC decision, residential bill impact, and large-load/data-center provisions with long-term commitments, minimum demand guarantees, financial protections, and cost-causation alignment.

sources.title: Data Centers in Virginia
sources.org: Virginia Joint Legislative Audit and Review Commission / Virginia RGA
sources.why_it_matters: State audit anchor for Virginia data-center incidence: energy-demand stress, all-customer cost exposure, stranded-infrastructure risk, water-planning gaps, local fiscal dependence, and the sales/use tax exemption that provided $928 million in FY23 tax savings and is used by about 90 percent of the industry.

sources.title: Data Centers and Water Use in the Potomac River Basin
sources.org: Interstate Commission on the Potomac River Basin
sources.why_it_matters: Basin-level water incidence anchor for Northern Virginia/Potomac data-center growth: current withdrawals and consumptive use, public-water-supplier reliance, absence of direct withdrawal permits to date, and 2050 average/peak demand projections under baseline cooling assumptions.

sources.title: Docket U-37425: Application for approval of generation and transmission resources in connection with service to a single customer for a project in North Louisiana
sources.why_it_matters: Official live docket surface for the Louisiana/Meta Richland Parish stack; confirms the docket is open and concerns generation and transmission resources for service to a single customer in North Louisiana.

sources.title: Entergy Louisiana receives LPSC approval for major infrastructure investments to support Meta’s data center and improve reliability
sources.why_it_matters: Utility/current-status source for the approved Louisiana/Meta infrastructure package: three combined-cycle gas facilities, new transmission facilities, and expedited procurement authority for up to 1,500 MW of solar resources, with the utility asserting Meta pays its share.

sources.title: Entergy Louisiana announces a new agreement with Meta that will deliver an additional $2B in customer savings
sources.why_it_matters: Utility/current-status source for the revised Meta agreement; asserts full cost-of-service recovery from Meta, about $2 billion in additional customer savings over 20 years, and about $2.65 billion in combined customer benefits.

sources.title: Direct Testimony of Catherine Kunkel on behalf of Alliance for Affordable Energy and Union of Concerned Scientists, LPSC Docket U-37425
sources.org: Alliance for Affordable Energy / Union of Concerned Scientists / LPSC docket filing
sources.why_it_matters: Adversarial docket testimony for the Louisiana/Meta case; identifies ESA term, CIAC, possible stranded-cost and net-energy-cost risks, and recommends commission review of final ESA terms, longer term protection, disallowance of pre-ESA costs if the project cancels, and FAC credits for non-Laidley customers.

sources.title: Motion for investigation of Meta/Blue Owl financing risks in LPSC Docket U-37425
sources.org: Alliance for Affordable Energy / Union of Concerned Scientists / Earthjustice / LPSC docket filing
sources.why_it_matters: Adversarial regulatory filing that raises financing and sponsor-risk questions after Blue Owl/Beignet restructuring; keeps the case from treating utility full-cost claims as dispositive without sponsor, lease-term, collateral, and abandonment-risk verification.

sources.title: Order No. U-37425 with Attachment A: settlement acceptance and customer-protection conditions for Meta/Laidley load
sources.why_it_matters: Official written order for the Louisiana/Meta U-37425 project; closes the written-order proof debt while showing that the generation/transmission certification is conditioned, the ESA and related agreements are not themselves approved, and ratepayer protections depend on CIAC, parent guaranty/collateral, early-termination, reporting, and transmission-cost conditions.

sources.title: Docket U-37882: Entergy Louisiana Project Evest application for generation and transmission resources
sources.why_it_matters: Official current docket surface for the adjacent Project Evest hyperscale-data-center expansion track in Richland Parish; keeps the Louisiana analysis from closing after U-37425 because a second project is already in an open certification docket.

sources.title: Entergy Louisiana U-37882 non-confidential public application for Project Evest certification under the Lightning Initiative
sources.org: Entergy Louisiana / Louisiana Public Service Commission docket filing
sources.why_it_matters: Project Evest application evidence: a second adjacent hyperscale data center, claimed $2.67 billion in benefits over a 20-year ESA term, proposed generation/transmission resources, and redacted HSPM/AEO terms that must be tested against ratepayer and public-balance-sheet protections.

sources.title: Order No. U-37882: procedural schedule for Project Evest certification record and December 16, 2026 Commission consideration
sources.why_it_matters: Official procedural order making Project Evest a time-bound live risk: the Administrative Hearings Division must compile the record and schedule the matter for Commission consideration at the December 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

sources.title: Docket X-37921: Louisiana large-load additions non-binding guidelines repository docket
sources.why_it_matters: Official statewide large-load policy router: the repository docket turns Louisiana data-center risk from a single-project issue into an evolving large-load-guidelines watch with no interventions accepted and policy/process change triggers.

sources.title: Large Load Additions Non-Binding Guidelines
sources.why_it_matters: Official Louisiana large-load scoring template. It converts the U-37882 and X-37921 watch from generic docket monitoring into twelve concrete proof categories: load shape, resource adequacy, transmission/interconnection, stranded asset/exit risk, rate design, curtailment, ancillary services, fuel infrastructure, load ramp, market/planning impacts, environmental/local impacts, and ongoing oversight. The guidelines are non-binding, but failure to address them is explicitly a utility risk.

sources.title: Direct Testimony of Phillip R. May, Project Evest U-37882 public redacted version
sources.org: Entergy Louisiana / Louisiana Public Service Commission docket filing
sources.why_it_matters: Project Evest executive testimony: identifies seven 1x1 CCCTs, three battery resources, major transmission including a 500/230kV interconnection substation and more than 250 miles of 500kV/230kV lines, roughly $13B generation capital, customer minimum-monthly-charge/FRP/FAC cost-coverage claims, already-made long-lead-item contributions, quarterly monitoring, and the caveat that final prudence is not determined by certification.

sources.title: Direct Testimony of Laura K. Beauchamp, Project Evest U-37882 large-load-guidelines mapping
sources.org: Entergy Louisiana / Louisiana Public Service Commission docket filing
sources.why_it_matters: Maps Project Evest against the LPSC large-load guidelines and is useful both affirmatively and as a redaction audit: it states that guideline failures can lead to certification refusal, lists the twelve categories, claims ESA/MMC/FAC/resource-plan protections, and repeatedly points core load, stranded-asset, and financial exhibits to HSPM/AEO sealed material.

sources.title: Notice of repository docket for Large Load Additions Non-Binding Guidelines, X-37921
sources.why_it_matters: Official X-37921 notice: it establishes a repository docket for comments on the guidelines, says no interventions will be accepted, sets a June 19, 2026 written-comment deadline, and points to a Staff report-back by December 2026. This makes the process a comment/repository watch rather than an adversarial contested-case proof source.

sources.title: Minutes of February 25, 2026 Business and Executive Session: directive on large-load non-binding guidelines
sources.why_it_matters: Official Commission-minute origin for the large-load guidelines: explains that the guidelines provide transparency on known areas of concern, will be part of Commission analysis in large-load proceedings, and points to the 2019 planning threshold for projected peak-load increases greater than 5% of prior peak load.

sources.title: Order No. X-37566: Annual Resource Adequacy Demonstrations
sources.why_it_matters: Official Louisiana resource-adequacy order. It gives concrete statewide summer/winter peak-load and reserve-margin forecasts and explicitly links sharp load-projection shifts to new industrial facilities, electrification, and the tech sector demand for large data centers and AI computing. This converts the Louisiana large-load case from project assertion into measurable capacity-stress context.

sources.title: May 7, 2026 Large Load Additions Technical Conference transcript
sources.why_it_matters: Official transcript for the Louisiana large-load technical conference. It clarifies that the Lightning Directive can waive the market-based mechanism but not Commission consideration/certification, explains the non-binding guideline purpose, and surfaces resource-adequacy, capacity, fuel, market-impact, and post-approval monitoring questions.

sources.title: Hut 8 SEC Exhibit 99.1: 15-year River Bend lease with Fluidstack and Google backstop
sources.org: Hut 8 Corp. / SEC EDGAR furnished exhibit
sources.why_it_matters: Direct public company disclosure for the River Bend project: a 15-year 245 MW critical IT NNN lease valued at $7.0B during the base term, up to $17.7B with renewals, a Google backstop for lease and pass-through obligations, ROFO rights for up to 1,000 MW of additional IT capacity, and expected loan-to-cost debt financing. This creates private cash-flow and sponsor/backstop evidence distinct from utility ratepayer protection.

sources.title: Hut 8 selects southeast Louisiana as site of $10 billion artificial intelligence data center
sources.why_it_matters: Official economic-development announcement for River Bend. It gives the public local-incidence framing: up to $10B phase-one investment, up to 1,000 MW utility capacity, Entergy Louisiana initial 330 MW utility capacity supporting 245 MW critical IT load, expected Q2 2027 operations, and anticipated data-center tax rebate and Quality Jobs incentives.

sources.title: Hut 8 SEC Exhibit 99.1: $3.25 billion River Bend senior secured notes pricing
sources.org: Hut 8 Corp. / SEC EDGAR furnished exhibit
sources.why_it_matters: Direct financing disclosure for River Bend: $3.25B investment-grade senior secured notes due 2042, fully amortizing, non-recourse to Hut 8 Corp., used to finance the 245 MW critical IT capacity project and substation, with first-priority liens on issuer assets. This is central to seniority analysis because private creditor protections may be well specified even when utility/ratepayer protections remain opaque.

sources.title: Hut 8 commits $16 million to expand water infrastructure in West Feliciana Parish
sources.why_it_matters: Company/parish water-infrastructure commitment for River Bend: $16M for a new well, about eight miles of water main, and other system enhancements to be transferred to the parish, with company claims of no taxpayer cost, closed-loop cooling, and no local water-supply impact. It narrows the water proof gap but remains a company-claim source until permits, agreements, drought rules, and operational withdrawals are visible.

sources.title: Hut 8 SEC Form 8-K: River Bend notes indenture and financing constraints
sources.why_it_matters: Direct SEC 8-K disclosure of the River Bend notes indenture: 6.192% senior secured notes due 2042, amortization from 2028, redemption tied to lease termination or DSCR stress, and covenant restrictions on additional debt, liens, lease and guarantee modifications, affiliate transactions, asset sales, sale-leasebacks, and unrelated operations. This converts River Bend private creditor seniority from a generic concern into a traceable contract-risk packet.

sources.title: River Bend project page
sources.why_it_matters: Company project-status page for River Bend: 330 MW utility capacity supporting 245 MW IT capacity, potential utility capacity of more than 1 GW, a 627-acre site footprint within 2,361 acres under option, and headline capital/jobs claims. This is useful for scale and siting, but remains company-side evidence rather than public cost-assignment proof.

sources.title: Louisiana R.S. 47:305.73: data center sales and use tax exemption
sources.why_it_matters: Current statutory authority for Louisiana data-center sales/use tax exemptions, including qualifying-capex and job thresholds, initial term and renewal structure, and termination/collection language. It turns River Bend public-incentive exposure from press language into a statutory exemption track that still needs award-level and clawback evidence.

sources.title: HB466 / Act 434: West Feliciana ad valorem tax rebate authority
sources.why_it_matters: Official Louisiana Legislature bill-status surface for HB466 / Act 434, signed by the Governor on May 29, 2026 with an effective date of January 1, 2027. It authorizes West Feliciana ad valorem tax rebates under stated conditions, making the River Bend property-tax/PILOT and rebate layer a current legal authority to track rather than a proposal.

sources.title: Hut 8 West Feliciana water, PILOT/rebate, and electric-infrastructure reporting
sources.org: New Orleans CityBusiness / The Center Square
sources.why_it_matters: Local reporting records project-specific claims about a $16M water-infrastructure contribution, closed-loop cooling/no-pressure-drop assurances, PILOT/rebate treatment, sales-tax benefits, and statements that switchyard/line/electric infrastructure would not be charged to ratepayers or taxpayers. These are high-value public-incidence claims that now require primary agreements and utility accounting proof.

sources.title: Policymakers Must Act to Protect Louisianans from Billions in Data Center-Driven Costs
sources.why_it_matters: Adversarial modeling estimate that data-center load could impose up to $26B in additional Louisiana electricity-system costs over 2026-2041, with separate public-health and climate-damage estimates. The cube uses it as a challenger model, not as official measurement, to stress-test utility and developer hold-harmless claims.

sources.title: Hut 8 selects Entergy, Southeast Louisiana for River Bend AI data center
sources.why_it_matters: Utility-side project announcement tying River Bend to Entergy Louisiana service: 330 MW of initial utility capacity for 245 MW of critical IT load, Fluidstack/Google backstop context, expected sales/use tax rebate and Quality Jobs participation, construction underway, and operations expected in Q2 2027. It narrows who the utility counterparty is while leaving tariff/ratebase proof unresolved.

sources.title: Data Center Deal Could Net Louisiana Parish $90M a Year
sources.why_it_matters: Local reporting on the West Feliciana Industrial Development Board/PILOT structure: up to $90M per year through a 30-year agreement, IDB ownership/leaseback, annual GPU valuation, and early Entergy substation/switchyard work. It gives a concrete local fiscal architecture to verify against primary IDB contracts.

sources.title: West Feliciana Parish approves schedule for distributing data center payments
sources.why_it_matters: Local meeting reporting that the West Feliciana Industrial Development Board approved a distribution schedule for Hut 8 PILOT proceeds and describes the property donation/leaseback mechanism and approximate allocation among parish, sheriff, school board, and smaller taxing bodies. It converts the public-upside claim into a distribution schedule proof target.

sources.title: Legislation would allow West Feliciana to rebate property taxes from data center windfall
sources.why_it_matters: Local reporting on the HB466/Act 434 rebate authority and the sequencing claim that infrastructure needs would come before any homeowner/property-owner credit. It helps distinguish gross PILOT revenue from actual public-upside delivery and rebate implementation proof.

sources.title: West Feliciana Parish Council and public records surfaces
sources.why_it_matters: Official parish surface for council meeting cadence, agenda/minutes availability, council authority, and public-records routing. It is not substantive proof of the Hut 8 terms by itself; it is the public-instrument ladder for obtaining missing IDB/PILOT, water, electric-infrastructure, and rebate records.

sources.title: West Feliciana Boards & Commissions: Industrial Development Board resolution route
sources.why_it_matters: Official parish surface listing an Industrial Development Board resolution adopted May 4, 2026 and identifying the IDB as the public board through which the River Bend PILOT/leaseback record must be obtained. The web surface gives a primary-record route but, by itself, does not expose the full resolution text or cooperative endeavor agreement.

sources.title: West Feliciana is getting a $10M advance from Hut 8. Here’s how it will be used
sources.org: 10/12 Industry Report / Baton Rouge Business Report
sources.why_it_matters: Recent local reporting on a special-meeting approval of a cooperative endeavor agreement for a $10M advance on Hut 8 PILOT payments, including allocation amounts, repayment timing, expected first regular payment, road/water uses, and pay-raise uses. It narrows the public-upside and implementation evidence but still requires the signed agreement and minutes.

sources.title: West Feliciana Parish Council and Industrial Development Board accept agreement for prepayment from data center
sources.why_it_matters: Local reporting on the West Feliciana council and IDB accepting a cooperative endeavor agreement for a Hut 8 PILOT prepayment, including July 1, 2026 timing, allocation amounts, reimbursement obligations, sign-off requirements, and deferral of a water-line servitude. It sharpens the implementation checklist but still requires primary agreements, minutes, payment proof, and servitude terms.

sources.title: August 20, 2025 LPSC Business and Executive Session transcript: U-37425 parent-guarantee and ratepayer-risk discussion
sources.why_it_matters: Official LPSC open-session transcript for U-37425 capturing public and commissioner discussion of cost-shift concerns, transmission and O&M/gas-risk allegations, and the enforceability of parent guarantees. It functions as contrary-evidence and reversal-rule input rather than proof that costs have actually shifted.

sources.title: Rev. Proc. 2025-32: tax year 2026 inflation adjustments and OBBBA estate/gift/GST amounts
sources.why_it_matters: Official revenue procedure line-locating the OBBBA amendment to §2010(c)(3), the $15,000,000 basic exclusion amount for 2026, the $15,000,000 generation-skipping transfer exemption amount, and inflation adjustment after 2026. It is the strongest primary current-law locator for the transfer-tax currentness case.

sources.title: IRS Estate tax page: filing threshold and portability election
sources.why_it_matters: Official current estate-tax page listing the $15,000,000 2026 filing threshold and the portability-election note for estates of decedents survived by a spouse. It separates filing threshold and portability from the bare BEA amount.

sources.title: IRS Gifts & Inheritances FAQ: annual gift-tax exclusion and Form 709 triggers
sources.why_it_matters: Official FAQ line-locating that the annual exclusion amount for 2025 and 2026 is $19,000 and that Form 709 is required for gifts above the annual exclusion or for future interests, split gifts, and certain spousal gifts. It prevents the transfer-tax case from conflating annual-exclusion reporting with lifetime BEA.

sources.title: IRS 2025-2026 Priority Guidance Plan: §2010 exemption regulations
sources.why_it_matters: Official guidance-plan source showing Treasury/IRS planned regulations under §2010 regarding extension and enhancement of increased estate and gift tax exemption amounts. It turns the transfer-tax currentness case into a guidance-watch lane rather than a one-time numeric update.

sources.title: Public Law 119-27: Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act)
sources.why_it_matters: Primary statutory current-law source for payment-stablecoin issuer reserve, no-federal-guarantee, no-deposit-insurance, and no-interest/yield perimeter. It is the decisive law-text anchor for the stablecoin backstop case, while final rules and implementation records remain open.

sources.title: Payment Stablecoins and Cross-Border Payments: Benefits and Implications for Monetary Policy Implementation
sources.org: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.why_it_matters: Federal Reserve policy note connecting payment-stablecoin use to payment rails, cross-border flows, monetary-policy implementation, and the GENIUS Act 1:1 value-stability framework. It supplies context, not a certification of stress loss allocation.

sources.title: Treasury Proposes Rule to Implement the GENIUS Act’s Requirements to Counter Illicit Finance
sources.why_it_matters: Official Treasury rulemaking release for treating permitted payment stablecoin issuers as BSA financial institutions with AML obligations and sanctions-program requirements. It helps bind the compliance perimeter but does not prove operational execution or crisis terms.

sources.title: OCC Bulletin 2026-24: GENIUS Act Reporting Forms and Instructions for Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers
sources.org: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
sources.why_it_matters: Official OCC current-release anchor for proposed weekly confidential and quarterly reporting forms for OCC-supervised permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers; it turns the issuer-data blocker into a concrete reporting-form checklist while remaining proposed and subject to change.

sources.title: OCC Reporting Form PS-01 Instructions: Payment Stablecoin Activity and Reserve Weekly Reporting
sources.org: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
sources.why_it_matters: Primary form-instruction source for the proposed weekly issuer data: daily issuance/redemption, reserve-asset composition, ownership concentration, trading activity, counterparties, secondary-market pricing, nonredeemable amounts, and redemption-timing measures.

sources.title: OCC Reporting Form PS-02 Instructions: Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuer and Foreign Payment Stablecoin Issuer Reports of Condition and Income
sources.org: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
sources.why_it_matters: Primary form-instruction source for proposed quarterly condition-and-income data, including income, balance sheet, off-balance-sheet activities, capital elements, and operational backstop assets.

sources.title: FDIC FIL-11-2026: Notice of Proposed Rulemaking to Establish GENIUS Act Requirements and Standards for FDIC-Supervised Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers and Insured Depository Institutions
sources.why_it_matters: Official FDIC supervisory currentness source for FDIC-supervised PPSI requirements: identifiable reserves, capital and risk-management standards, two-business-day redemption, custody/safekeeping, and the proposed no pass-through insurance treatment for reserve deposits.

sources.title: OFR Brief 26-02: Measuring Counterparty Exposures to Private Credit
sources.why_it_matters: Officially hosted OFR research brief that turns private-credit backstop risk into measurable counterparty channels: debt financing extended to private credit funds and LP capital commitments, while warning that fund identification is manual, resource-intensive, and imperfect.

sources.title: Form PF; Reporting Requirements for All Filers — SEC/CFTC Proposed Rule
sources.why_it_matters: Primary current-rulemaking source for Form PF drift: the proposal would raise the all-filer threshold, keep coverage of over 90% of private fund gross assets by estimate, add a method to identify private-credit-active funds, and keep Form PF information confidential rather than public claimant evidence.

sources.title: SEC and CFTC Extend Form PF Compliance Date to Oct. 1, 2026
sources.org: Securities and Exchange Commission / Commodity Futures Trading Commission
sources.why_it_matters: Official action establishing that the 2024 Form PF amendments were delayed to October 1, 2026, preserving a live reporting-currentness blocker for private-fund and private-credit visibility.

sources.title: Readout: Financial Stability Oversight Council Meeting on March 25, 2026
sources.org: U.S. Department of the Treasury / FSOC
sources.why_it_matters: Official FSOC meeting readout showing private credit was part of the quarterly financial stability monitor and that the Council simultaneously advanced proposed nonbank-designation guidance, useful as a monitoring-salience edge but not as a public-loss-allocation instrument.

sources.title: Rising hedge fund leverage affects monetary policy implementation
sources.why_it_matters: Official Federal Reserve Bank research explaining that leveraged Treasury basis and swap-spread trades have become a major source of repo funding demand; it quantifies hedge fund net repo borrowing at roughly $1.8 trillion by year-end 2025 and links that demand to secured-rate pressure.

sources.title: The Cross-Border Trail of the Treasury Basis Trade
sources.org: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.why_it_matters: Federal Reserve note showing that Cayman-domiciled hedge funds dominate recent Treasury basis-trade positions, that TIC data undercapture this activity through repo/sponsored-repo channels, and that the gap affects Financial Accounts measures of household Treasury holdings, saving, and net worth.

sources.title: Treasury Clearing Implementation
sources.why_it_matters: Official SEC implementation hub for Treasury clearing, including live compliance dates and implementation materials; it anchors cash-market and repo compliance timing without treating central clearing as already implemented.

sources.title: Hedge Fund Monitor: Short notional Treasury futures by contract
sources.why_it_matters: Official OFR Hedge Fund Monitor chart page identifying a public proxy for leveraged-fund short Treasury futures positions, compiled from CFTC Traders in Financial Futures data.

sources.title: Hedge Fund Monitor: Long and short U.S. Treasury exposures
sources.why_it_matters: Official OFR Hedge Fund Monitor chart page anchoring aggregate Form PF long and short U.S. Treasury exposures, including cash securities and derivatives, while noting confidentiality-driven blanks/nulls.

sources.title: Update on the SEC’s Work Toward Treasury Clearing Implementation
sources.why_it_matters: SEC implementation statement identifying unresolved Treasury-clearing issues, including exemptive relief, extraterritorial scope, outages/failed trades, customer protection, cross-margining, and liquidity/competition effects.

sources.title: Homeowners Insurance: Premiums Generally Tracked Inflation but Rose More in Disaster-Prone Areas
sources.why_it_matters: Current federal audit source for homeowners insurance affordability and availability, including disaster-risk premium gradients, state regulatory review timing, and policy-option limits.

sources.title: Flood Risk Mitigation: Reducing Fiscal Exposure and Improving Affordability
sources.why_it_matters: Current GAO testimony source tying NFIP affordability/solvency tension, repetitive-loss mitigation, and taxpayer fiscal exposure into one noncertifying public-backstop perimeter.

sources.title: Flood: We Need to Abate the Flooding Risk
sources.org: U.S. House Committee on Financial Services
sources.why_it_matters: Current congressional hearing source for NFIP borrowing authority, current debt, and multiple-loss-property public-cost salience; useful as a perimeter locator, not a final incidence verdict.

sources.title: National Flood Insurance Program's Reinsurance Program
sources.why_it_matters: Official FEMA source explaining that NFIP reinsurance transfers future exposure but does not reduce current NFIP Treasury debt; needed to distinguish risk-transfer from public-balance-sheet repair.

sources.title: Home insurance premiums influence mortgage delinquencies, relocations
sources.why_it_matters: Federal Reserve Bank research tying rising homeowners insurance premiums to mortgage-payment burden, relocation, credit-card stress, and mortgage delinquency; it connects climate-insurance pricing to household balance sheets and public/private mortgage guarantees.

sources.title: Citizens’ 2026 Multiperil Rates to Drop Statewide
sources.why_it_matters: Official Florida residual-insurer currentness source for rate reductions, policy-count decline, market-recovery claims, and remaining assessment-risk governance.

sources.title: California FAIR Plan
sources.why_it_matters: Official California insurance-regulator page explaining FAIR Plan role, governance, coverage availability, and recent coverage-limit changes; it helps separate private association governance from taxpayer exposure claims.

sources.title: Increased Risk, Complex Investment Landscape Require Prudent Pension Management Practices
sources.why_it_matters: Current public-pension investment chartbook for alternative-asset growth, fee/expense pressure, volatility, and transparency needs; it supports a fee/liquidity-risk perimeter but not a plan-level verdict.

sources.title: Four U.S. Public Pension Points To Watch In 2026
sources.why_it_matters: Current credit-risk report identifying contribution-volatility, private-equity/private-debt allocation, illiquidity, capital-call, fee, valuation, and disclosure risks in U.S. public pensions.

sources.title: National Data
sources.date_notes: Quick facts page active March 2025 with Q2 2024 Federal Reserve Flow of Funds asset figure and GASB/plan-reporting caveat.
sources.why_it_matters: Public pension aggregate data dashboard explaining trust-fund funding, GASB/financial-report basis, plan heterogeneity, and national asset scale; useful to prevent aggregate assets from being treated as certified adequacy.

sources.title: 2025 Retirement Security Report: Private assets deliver the strongest returns for retirees across America
sources.why_it_matters: Industry-side contrary/qualifying source arguing private equity has delivered strong net-of-fee long-run returns for many public pensions; included to keep the case from equating private markets with automatic harm.

sources.title: Tax Expenditures Fiscal Year 2027
sources.org: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Tax Analysis
sources.why_it_matters: Official Treasury tax-expenditure table and baseline locator for FY2027: current-law date, interaction caveat, top-ranked ten-year preferences, and beneficiary-incidence caveats.

sources.title: The Distribution of Major Tax Expenditures in 2019
sources.why_it_matters: CBO distributional analysis distinguishes high-income-skewed preferential-rate and deduction benefits from lower-income refundable credit benefits, preventing a one-way anti-tax-expenditure verdict.

sources.title: How the 2025 Reconciliation Act (Public Law 119-21) Will Affect the Distribution of Resources Available to Households
sources.why_it_matters: CBO/JCT current-law distributional route for Public Law 119-21, including tax changes, benefit changes, state fiscal responses, and other spending/revenue channels.

sources.title: Tax Expenditures
sources.why_it_matters: Official Treasury refresh route and definition page for annual tax-expenditure estimates, including the caveat that tax-expenditure estimates do not incorporate behavioral responses.

sources.title: The Three Largest Medicare Advantage Organizations Denied Requests for Long-Term Acute Care and Inpatient Rehabilitation at Some of the Highest Rates
sources.org: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General
sources.why_it_matters: Current HHS-OIG source showing high prior-authorization denial rates for post-acute long-term acute-care hospital and inpatient rehabilitation requests among the largest Medicare Advantage organizations; needed to convert MA denial risk from a generic care-access concern into a locator-bound claim-security edge.

sources.title: Medicare Advantage Organizations Overturned Nearly All Appealed Prior Authorization Denials for Skilled Nursing Facility Admission, Raising Concerns About Initial Denials
sources.org: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General
sources.why_it_matters: Current HHS-OIG source reporting SNF admission denial, appeal, and overturn rates among 19 MAOs; directly supports appeal-burden and remedy-access claim-security edges while requiring caution because the data are service-specific and time-bounded.

sources.title: 2027 Medicare Advantage and Part D Rate Announcement
sources.why_it_matters: Current CMS rate-announcement source for MA risk-score trend, chart-review/audio-only diagnosis policy, and risk-adjustment implementation; supports payment-integrity and trust-fund/premium incidence perimeter but not a plan-level overpayment finding.

sources.title: March 2026 Report to the Congress: Medicare Payment Policy
sources.why_it_matters: Current MedPAC statutory report route for Medicare Advantage status, coding intensity, favorable selection, payments, plan costs, and post-acute-care issues; included as an official congressional advisory source, not as self-executing proof of plan-level extraction.

sources.title: Medicare Advantage Insurers Made Nearly 53 Million Prior Authorization Determinations in 2024
sources.why_it_matters: Nonprofit analysis of CMS-reported MA prior authorization data for 2019-2024, giving system-scale request, denial, appeal, and overturn context; used as a measurement and method-bound volume source, not as an official adjudication.

sources.title: 2026 CMS Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs Proposed Rule
sources.why_it_matters: Current CMS proposed-rule source for electronic prior authorization, shorter decision timelines, public transparency metrics, and API reporting; supports a remedy/data pipeline but remains noncertifying until final rules, implementation, and outcome data are bound.

sources.title: Part C Reporting Requirements
sources.why_it_matters: Official CMS reporting-requirements route showing that Medicare Advantage organizations must develop, compile, evaluate, and report Part C data to CMS at specified reporting levels, timeframes, and data elements; this turns MA denial work from narrative concern into a contract-reporting acquisition problem.

sources.title: Contract Year 2026 Part C Reporting Requirements Technical Specifications
sources.why_it_matters: Official CMS technical specification defining organization-determination and reconsideration reporting, including completed decisions, favorable/partially favorable/adverse outcomes, and exclusions; this is the field dictionary for converting prior-authorization concern into extractable denial/appeal records.

sources.title: Part C and Part D Data Validation
sources.why_it_matters: Official CMS route for annual retrospective Part C/D reporting-data validation and contract-level Limited Data Set access after validation and CMS review; this is the acquisition path, but also a certification blocker because access, timing, and data-use limits keep the evidence from being public and plan-service-complete.

sources.title: Medicare Advantage / Part D Contract and Enrollment Data
sources.why_it_matters: Official CMS monthly contract, plan, enrollment, service-area, and contact-data repository; this supplies denominator and organizational-join keys for any MA denial, appeal, quality, risk-adjustment, and recovery ledger.

sources.title: Medicare Advantage Risk Adjustment Data Validation Program
sources.why_it_matters: Official CMS RADV program route stating CMS reviews whether diagnoses submitted for risk adjustment are supported by medical records and may collect overpayments for unsupported diagnoses; this is the payment-integrity recovery spine for MA public-upside work.

sources.title: Medicare Advantage Risk Adjustment Data Validation Documents and Data
sources.why_it_matters: Official CMS RADV documents/data route with audited-contract lists, audit methods, results, and overpayment spreadsheets by payment year; this is the contract-level audit/recovery join surface for MA payment-integrity certification.

sources.title: Part C Utilization Management Annual Data Submission
sources.why_it_matters: Official CMS route for annual MA submission of internal coverage criteria used by organizations and delegated entities to process prior authorizations for Medicare Part C services starting with the 2026 coverage year; it adds a criteria layer, while leaving outcome/harm and audit-tool gaps.

sources.title: Parts C and D Reporting Requirements Limited Data Set
sources.why_it_matters: Establishes that Parts C/D reporting-requirements LDS files contain raw datasets by reporting section as reported by contracts after validation/review; this is the acquisition row route, not a public certification result.

sources.title: Medicare Managed Care Appeals & Grievances
sources.why_it_matters: Defines the live managed-care appeals/grievance route and records the May 1, 2026 Part C IRE transition to C2C, anchoring the remedy-chain join.

sources.title: Appeals Decision Search (Part C and Part D)
sources.why_it_matters: Provides a decision-search route for reviewed appeals; useful for remedy and reason coding but not a denominator for all denials or unappealed cases.

sources.title: Part C and D Performance Data
sources.why_it_matters: Supplies contract/program quality and performance context, including display measures and Star Ratings tables/technical notes, so denial/payment rows cannot be read without quality context.

sources.title: CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule (CMS-0057-F)
sources.why_it_matters: Creates a future prior-authorization metrics/API route; the workbench treats it as implementation infrastructure until actual metric rows and API outputs exist.

sources.title: MA Denial Notice
sources.why_it_matters: Anchors the notice and appeal-rights surface for denied, discontinued, or reduced services; required notice is not proof of comprehension, timely care, or adequate remedy.

sources.title: Part C and Part D Program Audits
sources.why_it_matters: Official CMS program-audit route for MA/Part D audit process, protocols, results, audit/enforcement reports, and record-layout instructions. It is an accountability acquisition route, but CMS cautions that protocols and record layouts are used for audit/monitoring and do not by themselves interpret policy.

sources.title: Part C and Part D Enforcement Actions
sources.why_it_matters: Official CMS enforcement-actions route showing CMS authority to impose CMPs, intermediate sanctions such as suspension of marketing/enrollment/payment, and terminations when sponsors fail contract/program requirements or no longer meet Part C/D conditions. It supplies the public accountability/remedy rail for MA claim-security rows.

sources.title: Contract Year 2026 Policy and Technical Changes to the Medicare Advantage Program and Part D Final Rule (CMS-4208-F)
sources.why_it_matters: Official CMS CY2026 final-rule fact sheet: it restricts reopening approved inpatient admissions except for obvious error or fraud and closes MA appeals loopholes by clarifying concurrent decisions, provider notice, and enrollee appeal rights. It turns rev0374 appeal burden into concrete plan-obligation fields.

sources.title: Master Beneficiary Summary File Base A/B/C/D
sources.org: Research Data Assistance Center / Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
sources.why_it_matters: Data-documentation route for beneficiary-level enrollment and demographic fields needed to disaggregate MA claim-security rows, including race, reason for entitlement, dual eligible status, monthly Part C enrollment, Part C plan information, and Part D low-income cost-sharing indicators.

sources.title: Mapping Medicare Disparities Tool
sources.org: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Office of Minority Health
sources.why_it_matters: CMS OMH route for identifying disparities between Medicare subgroups, including racial and ethnic groups, across health outcomes, utilization, and spending; it gives the case a public subgroup-disparity context that must not be averaged away.

sources.title: Medicare Current Beneficiary Survey
sources.why_it_matters: CMS survey route for beneficiary-reported social and medical risk factors, utilization, health outcomes, access, and information not otherwise available through administrative data, linked with Medicare enrollment and claims.

sources.title: Medicare Advantage and Prescription Drug Plan CAHPS Survey
sources.why_it_matters: CMS MA/PDP CAHPS route for objective contract comparisons on consumer-important domains and publicly reported plan experience; it supplies beneficiary-experience context that must be joined, not used as a substitute for denial/remedy rows.

sources.title: Contract Year 2027 Medicare Advantage and Part D Final Rule
sources.why_it_matters: CMS CY2027 final-rule fact sheet stating that CMS is not implementing the Excellent Health Outcomes for All reward formerly called the Health Equity Index reward; this prevents the case from treating a near-term Star Ratings equity reward as an active corrective instrument.

sources.title: Some Medicare Advantage Organization Denials of Prior Authorization Requests Raise Concerns About Beneficiary Access to Medically Necessary Care
sources.org: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General
sources.why_it_matters: HHS-OIG case-file and physician-review study found that some MA prior-authorization and payment denials met Medicare coverage or MAO billing rules; it directly supports clinical-correctness, documentation-sufficiency, and manual/system-error guardrails.

sources.title: 2024 Medicare Advantage and Part D Final Rule (CMS-4201-F)
sources.why_it_matters: CMS final-rule fact sheet states that MA organizations must provide the same medically necessary care as Traditional Medicare and limits internal criteria to specified evidence and public availability conditions.

sources.title: 42 CFR Part 422 Subpart C — Benefits and Beneficiary Protections
sources.why_it_matters: Regulatory text gives the basic-benefit and payment-entitlement rails for MA organizations, including payment for services found on appeal to be owed and denial-reason specificity beginning in 2026.

sources.title: 42 CFR Part 422 Subpart M — Grievances, Organization Determinations and Appeals
sources.why_it_matters: Regulatory text supplies the appeal/effectuation remedy deadlines needed to test whether a reversal actually restored service, item, drug, or provider payment in time.

sources.title: Many Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Managed Care Plans Have Limited Behavioral Health Provider Networks and Inactive Providers
sources.org: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General
sources.why_it_matters: OIG found limited behavioral-health provider networks and inactive “ghost” providers in managed-care directories, directly blocking any MA access proof that relies only on listed network size.

sources.title: Medicare Advantage and Section 1876 Cost Plan Network Adequacy Guidance
sources.why_it_matters: CMS guidance defines MA network adequacy, HSD tables, contract-level/triennial and triggering-event reviews, ACC pass/fail outputs, ZIP Code failure reports, and exception logic; it is necessary but not sufficient for actual access.

sources.title: CY 2026 Technical Implementation Guide for the Medicare Plan Finder Provider Directory
sources.why_it_matters: CMS HPMS memo route publishes the CY2026 MA provider-directory implementation guide and sample FHIR bundle for Medicare Plan Finder, creating a directory data route that still requires accuracy/activity validation.

sources.title: Provider Directory API Frequently Asked Questions
sources.why_it_matters: CMS FAQ states that provider-directory information must be available to current/prospective enrollees and the public within 30 calendar days of receiving provider-directory information or an update; this is a timing rule, not proof of real appointment availability.

sources.title: A Lack of Behavioral Health Providers in Medicare and Medicaid Impedes Enrollees’ Access to Care
sources.org: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General
sources.why_it_matters: OIG found few behavioral-health providers in selected counties actively served Medicare/Medicaid enrollees, low treatment rates, and long travel for many enrollees; it makes active-provider and appointment-access fields required.

sources.title: The Inability To Identify Denied Claims in Medicare Advantage Hinders Fraud Oversight
sources.org: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General
sources.why_it_matters: OIG found that MA encounter records lack a definitive denied-claim indicator; adjustment codes are imprecise and the recommendation to require a denied-claim indicator remains open, so payment-restoration rows cannot be certified from encounter data alone.

sources.title: 2026 Medicare Advantage and Part D Rate Announcement
sources.why_it_matters: CMS finalized CY2026 MA payment policies with a projected 5.06 percent, over $25 billion, payment increase and explicit payment-factor rows; useful as current payment-context history but not claim-security proof.

sources.title: Ratebooks & Supporting Data
sources.why_it_matters: CMS ratebooks and supporting data provide the MA county-rate, rate-calculation, and risk-adjuster route needed to connect a plan/contract row to benchmark and payment context.

sources.title: Data — Medicare Advantage Rates & Statistics
sources.why_it_matters: CMS data route exposes 422.272 MA bid-pricing data from submitted MA organization bid pricing tools, creating a route to plan bids/rebates that must be joined to actual benefit use and claim security.

sources.title: Bid Forms & Instructions
sources.why_it_matters: CMS bid-pricing tools and instructions are the technical route for plan-submitted bids; a certification row must preserve bid/rebate assumptions rather than treating supplemental benefit availability as realized value.

sources.title: Medicare Advantage: Questionable Use of Health Risk Assessments Continues To Drive Up Payments to Plans by Billions
sources.org: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General
sources.why_it_matters: OIG found diagnoses reported only on HRAs and HRA-linked chart reviews, absent other 2022 service records, generated an estimated $7.5 billion in 2023 MA payments and raised both payment-validity and care-followup concerns.

sources.title: Medicare Advantage Risk Adjustment Data Validation Final Rule (CMS-4185-F2) Fact Sheet
sources.why_it_matters: CMS explains the RADV final rule, including recovery of improper risk-adjustment payments where diagnoses lack medical-record support and extrapolation beginning with payment year 2018.

sources.title: Encounter Skilled Nursing Facility
sources.org: Research Data Assistance Center / Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
sources.why_it_matters: ResDAC documents that the MA SNF encounter file contains plan/contract, diagnosis/procedure/RUG, dates, and organization NPI fields but no payment variables, making it a service-presence route rather than payment or denial proof.

sources.title: Encounter Carrier
sources.org: Research Data Assistance Center / Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
sources.why_it_matters: ResDAC documents that the MA carrier encounter file contains professional-service variables such as contract/PBP, diagnoses, HCPCS, service date, and rendering NPI but no payment information and is rarely used alone.

sources.title: Plan Characteristics
sources.org: Research Data Assistance Center / Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
sources.why_it_matters: ResDAC documents plan base, premium, tier, service-area, crosswalk, and SNP-contract subfiles plus contract/PBP linkage variables; these identify plan design but not actual benefit use or remedy.

sources.title: Benefits Data
sources.why_it_matters: CMS Benefits Data provides approved MA and Part D benefits information for organizations that submit bids; approved benefit design is necessary but not proof of use, access, or claim restoration.

sources.title: PBP Benefits - 2026
sources.why_it_matters: The 2026 PBP Benefits file is the current approved-benefit surface for plan benefit packages, but it remains an offering/design file rather than a furnished-service or paid-claim source.

sources.title: Medicare Advantage in 2026: Premiums, Out-of-Pocket Limits, Supplemental Benefits, and Prior Authorization
sources.why_it_matters: KFF summarizes 2026 MA plan benefits, premiums, prior authorization, and the current gap that supplemental-benefit use/spending data are not yet available to researchers or consumers and detailed prior-authorization data are not collected for those benefits.

sources.title: Supplemental benefits in Medicare Advantage
sources.why_it_matters: MedPAC explains that rebate allocations are projections that may not reflect actual use and estimates large MA rebate spending financed through Medicare trust funds and Part B premiums, making actual-use evidence mandatory.

sources.title: Agent Broker Compensation
sources.why_it_matters: CMS publishes plan/company/state/county-level independent-agent compensation amounts and explains initial and renewal-like payments, making broker compensation a required enrollment-provenance field rather than background context.

sources.title: Contract Year 2025 Medicare Advantage and Part D Final Rule (CMS-4205-F)
sources.why_it_matters: CMS finalized MA/Part D marketing compensation guardrails because excessive broker compensation and bonuses can steer beneficiaries based on agent/broker financial interests instead of health needs.

sources.title: Special Fraud Alert: Suspect Payments in Marketing Arrangements Related to Medicare Advantage and Providers
sources.why_it_matters: OIG warns that suspect MA marketing payments to agents, brokers, providers, and related parties can steer beneficiaries, distort plan choice, and selectively target or avoid costly enrollees.

sources.title: United States Files False Claims Act Complaint Against Three National Health Insurance Companies and Three Insurance Broker Organizations for Kickbacks Paid to Brokers and Discrimination Against Disabled Medicare Beneficiaries
sources.why_it_matters: DOJ alleges MA insurers and broker organizations exchanged illegal kickbacks for enrollments, steered beneficiaries to plans paying more regardless of suitability, and avoided disabled beneficiaries; allegations must be treated as nonfinal contrary-risk evidence until adjudicated.

sources.title: Misleading Marketing Practices in Medicare Advantage
sources.why_it_matters: OIG is actively examining aggressive and deceptive MA marketing, CMS complaints from 2020-2024, beneficiary harms, and agent/broker incentive structures, so certification must remain open until complaint and harm evidence is bound.

sources.title: Medigap May Be Elusive for Medicare Beneficiaries with Pre-Existing Conditions
sources.why_it_matters: KFF estimates most MA enrollees ages 65+ lack guaranteed Medigap issue protections beyond initial windows, making MA exit feasibility and underwriting barriers required lock-in fields after serious illness or claim failure.

sources.title: When can I buy a Medigap policy?
sources.org: Medicare.gov / Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
sources.why_it_matters: Medicare.gov identifies the federal six-month Medigap open-enrollment period and limited guaranteed-issue windows, creating the official exit-rights locator for a beneficiary locked into MA after claim failure.

sources.title: Medigap Protection and Plan Switching Among Medicare Advantage Enrollees With Cancer
sources.why_it_matters: A 2025 study of MA beneficiaries newly diagnosed with cancer found higher switching to Traditional Medicare in states with Medigap guaranteed issue protections, supporting exit-rights as an access-to-remedy variable.

score_mediated_exclusion_and_risk_pricin.why: Credit, tenant, employment, insurance, fraud, and algorithmic scores that convert prior hardship, data traces, or weak documentation into higher prices or blocked access.

consumer_reporting_and_specialty_reports.why: National and specialty consumer-reporting systems, credit invisibility, medical-debt reporting, dispute rights, adverse-action notices, and score repair.

tenant_employment_and_insurance_screenin.why: Tenant screening, employment background dossiers, credit-based insurance scores, insurance external data, and AI-model governance in gatekeeping markets.

surveillance_pricing_identity_and_public.why: Personalized pricing, identity theft/fraud flags, government identity verification, digital welfare, AI risk management, and public-benefit algorithmic decisions.

fresh_start_core.why: Legacy source cluster normalized during rev0319 so every coverage-map entry has the same object shape.

intergenerational_transfer_and_family_we.why: Inheritance, lifetime gifts, estate tax, trusts, probate, family law, guardianship, child support, estate recovery, and title finality as intergenerational wealth-order machinery.

inheritance_gifts_estate_tax_and_trusts_.why: Lifetime transfers, bequests, estate/gift/GST perimeter, retirement-account beneficiary stakes, and dynasty-trust shielding.

probate_heirs_property_and_estate_recove.why: Probate, intestacy, heirs property, partition protection, Medicaid estate recovery, and home-equity preservation after death or care need.

family_law_guardianship_and_fiduciary_co.why: Divorce, retirement-asset division, child support, guardianship, fiduciary abuse, elder exploitation, and counsel/remedy access.

public_balance_sheet_sovereign_backstops.why: Public debt, interest cost, fiscal risk registers, contingent liabilities, guarantees, public credit programs, deposit insurance, central-bank balance-sheet effects, and public backstop design.

social_insurance_pension_claim_security_.why: Social Security, Medicare, private pension insurance, public pension funding, pension replacement rates, and claim-security haircuts across cohorts.

housing_finance_credit_and_public_guaran.why: Federal credit programs, FHA mortgage insurance, GSE conservatorship/Treasury support, and credit-subsidy transparency as hidden public balance-sheet surfaces.

public_assets_sovereign_wealth_and_upsid.why: Sovereign wealth funds, fiscal stabilization, public asset governance, long-horizon investment, responsible investment, and claimant share in upside.
